123|
124|### What a `style` line means
125|
126|A user flow or a process may carry one `style` line, or several on nodes that share one pair. The composer reads it as meaning, not as paint:
127|
128|| Where it sits | Pair | What the board shows |
129||---|---|---|
130|| On an end | Light red | An error, in light red, with the pink outline |
131|| On an end | Any other pair | The goal, in light green, with the pink outline, and the spine runs to it |
132|| On a decision | Any pair | The decision keeps its light yellow diamond and takes the pink outline |
133|| On a step | Any pair | That step in focus, in light pink |
134|
135|Pick the node the board exists to explain first, then the line that says what it is. A user flow and a process each need one such line, because the board has no other way to say what the first glance is, and the check refuses a model without one. With no end styled, the end the longest path reaches is still the goal and the others leave the flow, but the goal then carries no outline. A `linkStyle` line passes the check and changes nothing on a composed board, because a connector's colour belongs to its kind, and it never counts as the accent. An architecture, a sequence, a state diagram, an ER diagram and a gantt chart take no `style` line, because their kinds already carry their colour, and the check refuses styling on an architecture.
136|
137|### The accent
138|
139|The first glance is the one node, message or task a reader should see within two seconds, and the accent is how the board says so. Three measures keep it first:
140|
141|- **A hue no kind uses.** The light pink pair belongs to the accent alone and every kind draws another pair. The nearest kind hues, light red at 52 degrees and light violet at 60, sit well clear of the accent's 319
142|- **Weight as well as colour.** A marked node or bar takes an 8 pixel outline against 2 for every other node and 4 for a critical bar, and a marked message takes 4 pixels against 2. On a greyscale copy pink and light blue are both just grey, so the line is what tells them apart. Weight times contrast on white puts 25.0 on the accent against 4.9 on the start pill and 12.6 on the heaviest other mark, the ring of an end state
143|- **The mark gate.** The pink stroke measures 3.13:1 on white, which only violet also clears, so it is the one outline on the board that holds at overview zoom
144|
145|The start pill keeps its light blue, because at those weights it cannot outweigh the accent in colour or in greyscale. What carries the accent depends on the type:
146|
147|| Type | What carries the accent | How the model says so |
148||---|---|---|
149|| User flow, process | A node: a step, a decision, the goal or an error end | A `style` line, which the check requires |
150|| Architecture, state, ER | A node | `%% focus: <id>`, optional |
151|| Sequence | A message | `%% focus: <number>`, the message's place in the order, optional |
152|| Gantt | A task or a milestone | `%% focus: <id or name>`, optional |
153|
154|A `%% focus:` line is a comment, so the Mermaid stays plain. It names one thing, and a second line, a name that matches nothing or a line on a user flow or a process is refused. Where a type carries no focus line the first glance is whatever the layout shows first, and the gate says so. A planned first glance is one thing, never a group such as the end states, and when the layout would show another first, the model names it with a focus line rather than promise a glance the board does not give.
155|
156|### Note palettes
157|
158|The composer and a note extension both set colour through the Plugin API, where FigJam recognises a colour as a palette swatch only when each channel is written as `hex/255`. A rounded decimal makes it a custom colour that the colour picker no longer offers.
159|
160|| Node | Palette |
161||---|---|
162|| Sticky | White `#FFFFFF`, gray `#E6E6E6`, green `#B3EFBD`, teal `#B3F4EF`, blue `#A8DAFF`, violet `#D3BDFF`, pink `#FFA8DB`, red `#FFB8A8`, orange `#FFD3A8`, yellow `#FFE299` |
163|| Section | White `#FFFFFF`, light gray `#F9F9F9`, light green `#EBFFEE`, light teal `#F1FEFD`, light blue `#F5FBFF`, light violet `#F8F5FF`, light pink `#FFF0FA`, light red `#FFF5F5`, light orange `#FFF7F0`, light yellow `#FFFBF0` |
164|| Label | Violet fill `#874FFF`, stroke `#5427B4`, white text, the one preset for numbered pins |
165|
166|Sticky colours keep FigJam's usual meanings: blue for discussion, yellow for a question, green for a positive, pink for a concern, red for a blocker and teal for a decision. One sticky colour per legend is the default, because the numbers already tell the stickies apart.
167|
168|---
169|
170|## 4. GATES
171|
172|| Gate | Threshold | Applies to |
173||---|---|---|
174|| Text on fill | 4.5:1 | Charcoal `#1E1E1E` on every fill the check accepts |
175|| Mark on canvas | 3.0:1 | A stroke that carries meaning, measured on a white canvas |
176|| Text on mark | 4.5:1 | The white digit on a label pin: 4.57:1 on violet `#874FFF` |
177|
178|### Recorded departures
179|
180|| Departure | Measures | Note |
181||---|---|---|
182|| Seven strokes on the canvas | 1.53:1 to 2.65:1 | Every stroke but violet and pink sits under the mark gate. They are FigJam's own pairs, kept so a reader can recolour them from the picker, and the check never lets colour carry meaning alone |
183|| The lane stroke `#B3B3B3` | 2.1:1 | A lane outline is a container edge, not a mark, and its label names it |
184|| Figma's blue label example | Not used | Its white digit on `#3DADFF` measures 2.44:1, under the text gate, so the label pin takes the violet preset |
185|| The saturated fills | Not accepted | FigJam sets white text on a saturated fill, which measures 1.85:1 on `#66D575`. Mermaid cannot set a text colour, and the generator's text colour on a saturated fill was never observed, so the check refuses them |
186|
187|The canvas is measured as white. FigJam's canvas is near white with a dot grid, and its exact value was not measured, so a stroke reads a little weaker on the board than the column says.
188|
189|---
190|
191|## 5. TYPE AND GRID
192|
193|sk-design-diagram's type ramp and grid carry over, because the composer sets the font itself. Every board uses one family at one scale, Inter unless a design names another. A family FigJam cannot load falls back to Inter with a warning:
194|
195|| Text | Size | Weight |
196||---|---|---|
197|| Title | 64 | Bold |
198|| Subtitle | 28 | Regular, wrapped at the diagram's width between 960 and 1440 pixels and then narrowed while it keeps its number of lines, so its lines come out even |
199|| Zone and key names | 24 | Semi Bold |
200|| Node label | 20 | Medium |
201|| Edge label, key entry, source line | 18 | Medium on a connector, Regular elsewhere |
202|| Entity field | 16 | Regular |
203|| Gantt bar length, step pin | 14 | Medium |
204|
205|Every position and size sits on an 8 pixel grid. A shape grows from its kind's base size until its label fits inside it, with a 32 pixel inset in a round shape whose text FigJam clips to the inscribed box, and every shape of one kind on a board takes the size of the largest, so a rank reads as one row.
206|
207|The scale is tuned for a laptop at overview zoom. Reading distance does not change it, as `references/flow-mode.md` Section 4 sets out, and buys fewer nodes and shorter labels instead.
208|
209|A design re-maps meanings onto the pairs in Section 3 and never adds a colour. A board is shared and recoloured in FigJam, so a brand palette would turn every swatch into a custom colour. A brand colour asked for by name is a hand edit after the write, and the reply says it is off-palette.
210|
211|---
212|
213|## 6. WHAT HOLDS THE RECORD
214|
215|- `scripts/figjam_checks/common.py` holds the pairs the check accepts
216|- `assets/figjam-design.md` holds the design a board is drawn in, and `scripts/figjam_checks/design.py` reads it, checks every token against its floor and sends the composer only what differs from the built-in design
217|- `assets/compose-board.js` holds the built-in design, the swatches, the tints and the shapes, and `scripts/compose_board.py --self-test` measures the accent's hue, weight and ink on every board it composes and fails when the design file leaves out a token or breaks a floor
218|- `scripts/compose_board.py --design-check` prints the resolved design with its measured ratios and names every design warning
219|- The self-test fails when the record above names a pair the check does not accept, or the check accepts one the record does not name
220|- The self-test re-measures both ratio columns of every row and fails on any drift
221|
222|---
223|
224|## 7. SPACING
225|
226|Colour tells a reader what belongs together, but space tells them first. A reader groups what sits close before reading a label, so a board that spaces every gap the same reads as one flat field and its own structure disappears.
227|
228|| Band | Gap | What the gap separates |
229||---|---|---|
230|| One thought | 60 to 92 pixels | Two nodes a reader takes as one step or one idea |
231|| Same topic | 200 to 400 pixels | Two groups the board discusses one after the other |
232|| Another part of the board | 1000 pixels or more | Content that answers a different question |
233|
234|Two rules follow from the bands:
235|
236|- Two unrelated groups are never closer than the text blocks inside a card, so the gap between groups always reads wider than the gap within one
237|- A wrapper is larger than the group's own internal gap and smaller than the gap to the next group, so its edge never falls on a neighbour
238|

rank of six steps or a connector that doubles back, is caught here rather than

Each Mermaid block in the file is one diagram, read by its header:

- `flowchart` is a user flow unless a `%% type: process` or

**`get_figjam` is the inspection tool for FigJam files.** It returns the full node tree as XML, including IDs of pages, sections, stickies, connectors, and other nodes you need to reference in subsequent `use_figma` calls.
